transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-10
Time: 14:00 PDT
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Ava Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Sara Thompson (AtlasFin Head of ML), Ethan Ruiz (Infra Lead), Priya Menon (Security)

Auto-generated summary: Discussed benchmark methodology for runtime/VPC/KV cache/batching/quant. Next steps captured at end.

00:00:05 - Ava Patel: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll get started. quick intro - i'm ava, i'm the AE working with atlasfin, and liam is our SE who will run through the perf bits.
00:00:17 - Sara Thompson: thanks ava, appreciate it. we want to make sure the benchmark results we run are apples-to-apples with our onprem setup and when we evaluate redwood's dedicated offering.
00:00:26 - Liam Chen: totally. goal for today is to align on prompt sets, load gen, metrics (p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/sec), and the configs to keep constant - model variant, precision, seq length, batch size, and kv cache settings.
00:00:40 - Ethan Ruiz: quick callout from infra - network egress & VPC peering can add jitter. we'll need to capture end-to-end plus server-side timings.
00:00:49 - Priya Menon: also from security - we need to confirm how logs/audit are retained, and KMS key flow for private deployments.

00:01:12 - Liam Chen: ok jumping in. first principle: apples-to-apples means we compare the same model checkpoint and same numerical precision (eg fp16 vs int8) and same context length. quantized runs should be compared against fp16 baseline with quality evals.
00:01:28 - Sara Thompson: when you say quantized, you mean llm.int8 style quant? is that supported in the runtime?
00:01:34 - Liam Chen: yes we support several quant profiles - static int8, q4/8 variants, and mixed precision fp16. performance gaps depend heavily on kernel selection and NV driver versions. sometimes qos differs between A100 and H100. we've seen int8 reduce latency by ~25-40% in some seq lengths, but you must run quality evals.
00:01:58 - Ethan Ruiz: are those numbers on dedicated GPUs? our onprem has A100 40GB and older gen cards, so curious about warmup behavior.
00:02:06 - Liam Chen: correct - those were Dedicated benchmarks. on-prem with older cards you'll see slower kernel perf and possibly lower KV cache throughput. that brings up kv cache: if you get high prefix reuse, effective latency per request is much lower because a large portion of tokens are cache hits. we need to measure cold-start vs warmed cache.
00:02:28 - Sara Thompson: how do you instrument cache hit rate?
00:02:31 - Liam Chen: we produce per-request metrics that include cache_hit_ratio and cached_tokens. for the harness we'll include a flag to produce a breakdown: cold first request latency, steady-state with X% cache hit, and cache decay tests.
00:02:48 - Ava Patel: note - the harness repo we'll share has examples for 0%, 25%, 50%, 75% cache hit workloads so you can see the delta.
00:02:58 - Priya Menon: can you also log whether cached entries are from prefix caching vs kv kv cache? sometimes the naming in our logs is inconsistent and audit needs clarity.
00:03:07 - Liam Chen: yeah we'll standardize labels - prefix_cache vs kv_cache in the logs.

00:03:30 - Ethan Ruiz: load generation - you suggested locust/jmeter earlier? what's the recommended way to simulate realistic parallel sessions vs burst traffic?
00:03:38 - Liam Chen: we recommend a two-part approach: steady-state load to hit 90% of target throughput to measure p95, plus burst/spike tests to validate tail latency and autoscaling. Locust is good for scenario-based user simulation; for pure token throughput we provide a lightweight golang harness that drives concurrent streams with configurable think-times and seq lengths.
00:03:58 - Sara Thompson: for seq lengths - we have mixed short prompts (50 tokens) and long context completions (1k tokens). Should we run separate suites?
00:04:07 - Liam Chen: yes. separate prompt buckets: short (0-128), medium (129-512), long (513-2048). each bucket should be benchmarked independently because batching behavior and memory/KV usage differ.

00:04:33 - Ava Patel: quick note on batching - continuous batching helps throughput but can increase p95 if you wait to fill a batch. the runtime has latency-targeted batching modes (max_wait_ms) vs throughput-optimized batching. pick knobs that mirror your production SLOs.
00:04:46 - Ethan Ruiz: can we measure the tradeoff? like throughput at max_wait_ms=5 vs =50?
00:04:51 - Liam Chen: yes we'll include runs for a matrix of max_wait_ms and target batch size. we also instrument per-batch composition and per-token time.

00:05:10 - Sara Thompson: apples-to-apples also requires same tokenizer and byte pair encoding steps. if tokenization differs slightly, per-token metrics will be off. how do you ensure parity?
00:05:19 - Liam Chen: we ship the tokenizer used for each model in the harness and recommend you run tokenization locally to compare token counts. we also include a token-diff checker to flag mismatches in the prompt set.

00:05:34 - Priya Menon: security question - for Private (VPC/on-prem) where does the KMS call happen? do we ever route keys outside customer VPC?
00:05:42 - Ava Patel: for Private we support customer-managed keys; KMS integration can be configured to stay within your cloud account or HSM on-prem. we'll send the KMS integration doc.
00:05:50 - Priya Menon: perfect. and SOC 2 evidence?
00:05:53 - Ava Patel: yes we'll attach SOC 2 Type II and ISO materials in the follow-up.

00:06:08 - Liam Chen: back to metrics - recommended primary metrics: tokens_per_second (server-side), requests_per_second, p50/p95/p99 latency (server and end-to-end), cache_hit_ratio, GPU_utilization, memory_pressure, and per-token latency breakdown. include model quality metrics (BLEU/ROUGE or human evals) for quant runs.
00:06:25 - Ethan Ruiz: do you capture GPU power and temperature? our ops cares about cost and thermals on-prem.
00:06:29 - Liam Chen: yes harness can collect nvidia-smi snapshots, power draw, and driver versions. we'll standardize driver/OS labels in the artifact.

00:06:47 - Sara Thompson: about quantization: if we run int8 on redwood dedicated and compare to our fp16 on-prem, is that fair?
00:06:53 - Liam Chen: it's only fair if you also run int8 on your hardware or run fp16 on Redwood. apples-to-apples means same precision. if hardware doesn't support int8 kernels efficiently, mention that explicitly in the report. we'll include a comparison table template for that.

00:07:22 - Ava Patel: suggestion: baseline runs (fp16 on both sides), then optional accelerated runs (int8 on both sides). quality regression tests must be identical prompt sets and scoring.

00:07:34 - Ethan Ruiz: latency SLOs - sara, what are you targeting?
00:07:38 - Sara Thompson: p95 around 350ms for short prompts, <1s for mediums. long completions are less strict but we'd like stable throughput.
00:07:46 - Liam Chen: noted. we'll configure the harness to flag regressions against those thresholds.

00:08:03 - Liam Chen: a tricky point: warmup & cache population. if you seed the kv cache artificially, you get optimistic numbers. we recommend two canonical tests: truly cold (start from fresh, measure first N requests) and steady-state with a realistic session replay to populate cache, measure after X minutes.
00:08:21 - Sara Thompson: how long to run steady state?
00:08:24 - Liam Chen: depends on workload; common is 30-60 minutes for stable metrics, but for catalogs with high reuse you might see stability in 10-15 minutes. we'll provide guidance in the runbook.

00:08:43 - Ava Patel: let's discuss artifacts to share: harness repo link, runbook, sample prompt sets, result dashboard template (CSV/JSON + Grafana panels), and a benchmark report template with an apples-to-apples comparison matrix.
00:08:55 - Sara Thompson: please include example perf spreadsheets with side-by-side rows for model, precision, hardware, batch size, max_wait, cache_hit_rate, p95, tokens/sec, quality score.

00:09:10 - Ethan Ruiz: network noise - for VPC tests we should capture RTT distribution and also the effect of TCP windowing; any recommended network config?
00:09:18 - Liam Chen: pin MTU, use ENIs with enhanced networking when possible, and capture packet loss metrics. we'll include a network checklist for VPC and onprem lab.

00:09:35 - Priya Menon: compliance - can we get an architecture diagram showing data flow for Private?
00:09:39 - Ava Patel: yes we'll send an annotated diagram and indicate which components hold PII and which are ephemeral.

00:09:56 - Sara Thompson: a couple of tiebreaker questions - what's your recommendation for batch sizes for short prompts? we worry about queueing latency if batch size is too high.
00:10:06 - Liam Chen: for short prompts, smaller batch sizes (2-8) with low max_wait (<=5ms) keep latency low while still getting batching gains. for throughput runs you can push to larger batch sizes but tail latency increases. we'll run a matrix to find your sweet spot given your SLOs.

00:10:34 - Ava Patel: ok let's map next steps now so we have clear owners. liam will share harness + example scripts; ava will send security docs and pricing; sara will share prompt sets and SLOs; ethan will provision a VPC test environment and give us access creds or ephemeral VPN; priya will list compliance questions.
00:10:58 - Sara Thompson: timeline - can we aim to start the pilot next monday?
00:11:02 - Ava Patel: we can aim for a kickoff on 2026-07-13, pilot runs 7/13-7/20. is that workable?
00:11:07 - Ethan Ruiz: yes, we'll try to have the VPC prepped by end of week.
00:11:12 - Priya Menon: i'll compile a short compliance q list and send by tuesday.

00:11:30 - Liam Chen: small tech note - for reproducibility include seed values for randomness in generation and disable any sampling temperature variance unless you want to evaluate generation diversity.
00:11:40 - Sara Thompson: good point. we'll run deterministic runs for perf and separate stochastic runs for quality.

00:11:55 - Ava Patel: any final questions?
00:12:02 - Ethan Ruiz: one last thing - can the harness produce a single consolidated CSV with per-run metadata so we can upload into our internal analytics?
00:12:09 - Liam Chen: yes the harness outputs per-run JSON and a combined CSV summary; we'll include a mapping for column meanings.

00:12:22 - Ava Patel: great. we'll follow up with the repo link, runbook, SOC2, KMS notes, and proposed pilot schedule. thanks everyone.
00:12:31 - Sara Thompson: thanks ava and liam. excited to see the results.
00:12:35 - Priya Menon: thanks.
00:12:37 - meeting_end
